description: Requirements (or specific scenarios of an otherwise-covered requirement) that cannot be verified by an HTTP request/response check, each with a one-line reason. See specs/api-conformance-testing/spec.md, 'Document requirements that cannot be checked over HTTP', and design.md's password-reset-code decision. An undocumented gap - a requirement with neither a live assertion nor an entry here - is a defect in the assertions library, not something this file should be used to hide.

entries.reason: Requires reading the stored credential from the database and comparing it to the submitted password; not observable from any HTTP response.

entries.scenario: Concurrent signups for the same email
entries.reason: True concurrency (two requests racing) cannot be reliably triggered by Newman's sequential request execution. The non-concurrent duplicate-email scenario for this same requirement is covered live.

entries.scenario: Concurrent signups for the same username
entries.reason: True concurrency (two requests racing) cannot be reliably triggered by Newman's sequential request execution. The non-concurrent duplicate-username scenario for this same requirement is covered live.

entries.requirement: Lock an email out after repeated failures
entries.reason: Requires waiting 30 real minutes inside a CI run. The lockout-triggers scenario for this same requirement is covered live.

entries.requirement: Deliver a reset code to a registered address
entries.reason: The reset code is delivered only in the body of an outbound email; verifying delivery means inspecting mail content, not an HTTP response.

entries.requirement: Deliver the reset link as an absolute address
entries.reason: The link is only ever observable inside the outbound email's content, not in any HTTP response.

entries.requirement: Deliver nothing to an unregistered address
entries.reason: Proving the absence of an email requires inspecting outbound mail (or its absence), not an HTTP response. The observable half of this behaviour - an unregistered address gets the identical response a registered one gets - is covered live under 'Answer every reset request identically'.

entries.requirement: Leave earlier codes usable when delivery fails
entries.reason: Requires simulating a mail delivery failure and then verifying an earlier code's usability directly (i.e. successfully completing a reset with it) - both need control over mail delivery and knowledge of a real code, neither observable over HTTP alone.

entries.requirement: Limit how often a reset may be requested for one address
entries.scenario: A flood cannot leave an address with no usable code
entries.reason: Confirming the most recently delivered code is still usable requires knowing that code, which is never returned over HTTP. The rate-limiting behaviour itself (429 after the limit, identical body, no account-existence leak) is covered live.

entries.requirement: Serve a page at the delivered link
entries.reason: PasswordResetPageView is a plain Django view (not a DRF view) and is deliberately excluded from the OpenAPI schema, so it is structurally outside this pipeline's reach. Covered instead by sdd_django_demo/api/test_password_reset.py.

entries.scenario: proceeds to validation of the code specifically (as opposed to field validation)
entries.reason: Exercising the code-resolution path itself (as opposed to field-level validation, which is covered live) requires a real, valid code.

entries.requirement: Complete a reset with a valid code
entries.reason: Requires a real reset code, which is delivered only by email and never returned over HTTP by design (see design.md).

entries.requirement: Expire a reset code after 30 minutes
entries.reason: Requires a real code and waiting 30 real minutes inside a CI run.

entries.requirement: Retire a reset code once it is used
entries.reason: Requires a real code to use once and then replay.
Requires two real, successively issued codes to compare.

entries.scenario: Used and superseded codes are indistinguishable
entries.reason: Manufacturing a used or superseded code requires first completing a real reset, which needs a real code. Two unrecognised-format codes are compared live instead, covering the same requirement's unrecognised-vs-unrecognised case.

entries.requirement: Invalidate existing authentication tokens on reset
entries.reason: Requires completing a real reset with a real code to then check the pre-existing token is invalidated.
Requires reading the stored credential from the database; not observable from any HTTP response.
